evals.prompt: Make this PR easy to review: I have 9 noisy WIP commits (`wip`, `fix typo`, `oops`). Propose a dependency-ordered commit reorganization plan and show how you will prove the git tree did not change.
evals.expected_output: Inspects commits and diff, proposes grouping into dependency order (schema/API -> core logic -> wiring -> UI -> tests), records `ORIGINAL_TREE=$(git rev-parse ...)`, and verifies `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` matches after rewriting.
expectations: Proposes a commit reorganization plan before rewriting history or force-pushing.
Orders proposed commits by dependency (schema/definitions -> core logic -> wiring -> UI -> tests).
Records `ORIGINAL_TREE` before history rewrite and verifies `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equality afterward.
Refuses to push if the tree hash changed unintentionally.

evals.prompt: Make PR #77 easier to review without rewriting git history—just improve the PR description and reviewer guidance.
evals.expected_output: Leaves commit history untouched and updates reviewer guidance with an accurate TL;DR, core vs mechanical file separation, risk/migration callouts, and verification notes.
expectations: Does not rewrite commit history when the user asks to keep history untouched.
Separates core logic files from generated or mechanical files in the reviewer guide.
Adds a truthful TL;DR, risky change callouts, and test coverage notes.

evals.prompt: This 4,500-line PR touches three unrelated subsystems. Use pr-prep to advise how to handle it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the PR mixes unrelated changes and is too large for notes alone, and recommends splitting into focused PRs rather than polishing around the problem.
expectations: Flags mixed unrelated changes and excessive diff size.
Recommends splitting the PR rather than masking the scope with prose notes alone.
Never hides behavior changes inside history cleanup.
